entities.summary: Vincent Michael Conçessao is a prominent Indian Catholic clergyman who was installed as the fifth Archbishop of Delhi in November 2000. He served as Vice President of the Catholic Bishops' Conference of India from 2000 to 2004.

entities.summary: Vincent Michael Conçessao, a prominent Indian Catholic clergyman, played a pivotal role in shaping the country's religious landscape. Born on September 28, 1936, in Mangaluru, Karnataka, Conçessao rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church to become the fifth Archbishop of Delhi in November 2000. During his tenure, he focused on promoting interfaith dialogue and social justice, earning him recognition as a leading figure in Indian Catholicism. Conçessao's legacy extends beyond his own archdiocese, as he helped to foster greater understanding between Christians and Muslims in India. His contributions to the Catholic Church in India have had a lasting impact on the country's social and religious fabric. The Indian government's recognition of the importance of religious diversity has been a direct result of Conçessao's efforts. Conçessao's influence can be seen in the growing number of interfaith initiatives and organizations in India, which have become a cornerstone of his legacy. Conçessao's dedication to social justice has inspired a new generation of Indian Catholics to become involved in activism and community service. Conçessao's commitment to promoting religious understanding has made a significant difference in the lives of millions of people in India.
